title: Complete summary – Physics, X-rays, radiographic image, contrast & radioprotection
html:
Built by reverse-engineering every MCQ of this lecture (exams 2022, 2023, 2025, old exam, practice sets). 🔁 = asked in several sessions · ⚠ = classic trap.

X-rays: nature and properties

  • Electromagnetic waves (photons) → propagate at the speed of light, in a straight line, spreading spherically/divergent; the beam is CONIC (shaped by the collimator/diaphragm) 🔁
  • Intensity decreases with distance (inverse-square law).
  • Attenuation depends on atomic number (Z), density and thickness of the tissue (and beam energy) – NOT on the object–film distance ⚠
  • High absorption coefficient = high Z (bone, calcium, iodine, barium, metal) → strongly attenuates → white on the film; CT density high (bone +400 to +1000 HU), not 50–150 HU ⚠

Production – the X-ray tube

  • Heated cathode filament emits electrons → accelerated by the voltage → hit the anode.
  • Main mechanism: braking radiation (bremsstrahlung) = continuous spectrum, the main component of the beam.
  • Characteristic radiation: inner-shell electron ejected, outer-shell electron fills the gap → fixed energy specific to the anode material; discrete, minor part ⚠
  • ~99 % of the electron energy becomes heat.
  • kV = energy / penetration; mAs = quantity of photons.

Effects of X-rays 🔁

  • Used in imaging: penetration, photochemical (film blackening), photoelectric, luminescence = fluorescence / phosphorescence (intensifying screens, image intensifier), ionisation, biological effect.
  • NOT effects: photosynthesis ✗, fluoroscopy ✗ (it is a technique), radiofrequency signal ✗ (MRI) ⚠
  • Phosphorescent (fluorescent screen) effect → used in film-screen radiography (intensifying screens) and fluoroscopy.

Interaction with matter & scatter

  • Relevant in diagnostic range: photoelectric absorption, Compton scatter, coherent (Rayleigh) – minor. Pair production (> 1.02 MeV) and fission: no.
  • Scatter (Compton) is reduced by an anti-scatter grid and by collimation (small field). Increasing kV, removing the collimator or a large field ↑ scatter.

Image geometry – sharpness & magnification 🔁🔁

  • Object FAR from the film → image LARGER (magnified) and more BLURRED (imprecise edges). The image IS influenced.
  • Sharp image with near-real size: object as CLOSE as possible to the film, small focal spot, long focus–detector distance, no movement.
  • PA chest: heart closer to the film → less magnified than on AP.

Vocabulary and reading 🔁🔁

TechniqueWord
Radiography, fluoroscopy, mammographyOpacity (white) / transparency (black)
CT (also unenhanced)Density (hyper/hypo-dense, HU)
MRISignal (hyper/hypo-intense)
UltrasoundEchogenicity
  • Projection = path of the X-ray beam through the body (AP / PA), NOT the anatomical plane, region or film size ⚠
  • Reading: as if facing the patient → patient's left on the viewer's right.
  • Standing patient → PA chest (standard); bedridden → AP.
  • Describe a lesion: number, location, size, shape, contour, opacity/density, structure, relations. NOT stiffness (elastography) or vascularity (Doppler).
  • Radiograph quality: patient ID (name, age, date), adequate penetration (vertebrae visible behind heart), correct positioning/no rotation, gonadal protection.

Techniques – ionising or not 🔁

  • Ionising: radiography, fluoroscopy, CT, urography, mammography, angiography, nuclear medicine.
  • Non-ionising: ultrasound, MRI (preferred in pregnancy).
  • Fluoroscopy: real-time, X-rays, image intensifier/flat panel, used for barium studies and interventions; relatively high cumulative dose.
  • Digital radiography: post-processing (window, zoom), PACS archiving, teleradiology, fewer repeats, usually lower dose.

Contrast media 🔁🔁🔁

  • Positive (white): barium, iodine. Negative (black): air, CO₂, water (in gastric CT).
  • Barium → digestive tract (highly diluted barium may be given). Contraindicated: suspected perforation (use water-soluble iodine), acute digestive inflammation, large-bowel obstruction (oral route).
  • Iodine → CT, intravenous urography (given i.v.), angiography.
  • Gadolinium → MRI: shortens T1 (bright on T1); extracellular or hepatospecific (gadoxetic acid / Primovist); NSF in severe renal failure; pregnancy: avoided unless essential (not absolute).
  • US contrast = microbubbles; not used in pregnancy.
  • CT liver ("hepatic/portal") phase ≈ 45–60(–70) s, not 1–1.4 min ⚠

Iodinated contrast – kidney rules (asked every year)

eGFR (ml/min/1.73 m²)Rule
< 30Contraindicated (absolute, unless vital)
30–50Relative – hydration
50–80Possible with adequate hydration ✓
  • Absolute contraindications: eGFR < 30, acute kidney failure, previous severe reaction to iodine, untreated HYPERthyroidism. NOT: allergic disease in general, pregnancy, hypothyroidism ⚠
  • Adverse reactions of iodine: anaphylactoid reactions, contrast-induced AKI, thyrotoxicosis (iodine, NOT MRI), extravasation. NSF = gadolinium.
  • Contrast-induced AKI can occur with contrast CT AND contrast MRI.
  • Abdominal CT: i.v. contrast is mandatory to characterise a liver nodule; NOT mandatory for bowel occlusion or pneumoperitoneum (free air seen without contrast, lung window).

Radiobiology & radioprotection 🔁🔁

  • Principles: justification, optimisation (ALARA), dose limitation. Stochastic/deterministic = effects, dosimeters = tools – not principles ⚠
  • Deterministic: threshold, severity ∝ dose, e.g. cataract, skin erythema, skin lesions after interventional radiology; NOT common after diagnostic CT.
  • Stochastic: no threshold, probability ∝ dose → cancer (appears after years, not 1–2 years); children more sensitive.
  • With modern radioprotection, radiologists have no significant excess cancer risk.
  • Acute radiation syndrome: haematopoietic, gastrointestinal, cerebrovascular (+ skin) – NOT respiratory.
  • Staff protection: time ↓, distance ↑, shielding (lead aprons); dosimeter monitors exposure.
  • CT dose depends on mAs, kV, pitch/table speed, slice thickness/collimation, scan length, number of phases. Lower dose: large pitch, medium kV/mAs; thin slices and max mAs ↑ dose.
